_comment: On-device regression matrix for the webOS Plex player. Each case drives the app headless via plxnative-* triggers inside that install's runtime root (make -s print-rundir FLAVOR=<f>; see README) and asserts on plxnative-events.log there. This file is INSTALLATION-INDEPENDENT: a case names the SHAPE of the item it needs (`item`, a symbolic key) and never a ratingKey. tests/manifest.local.json — gitignored, copy it from manifest.local.json.example — maps those keys to items on YOUR server and carries the pms host, tv address and test_user with them; run.py merges it over this file at load and refuses to run without it, naming any key it cannot resolve. The X-Plex-Token is read from src/config.local.h at runtime — it is NEVER stored in either file. Cases are derived from a survey of one real library; see library_gaps for combos no item in it could cover.
_shared_server_comment: A case or fps scene that needs the app to hold TWO servers' credentials (a friend's SHARED server beside your own — its own machineIdentifier, its own access token, a 401 for anybody else's) declares `"needs_shared_server": true` here. That is installation-INDEPENDENT: WHICH server is named in manifest.local.json's optional `shared_server` block, and its access token is resolved from plex.tv at run time (nothing is stored). run.py then writes plxnative-servers beside plxnative-token in that install's runtime root — the app parses it in dev::servers() and logs `servers: <n> extra server(s) injected, <n> usable`, never a token. An installation with no `shared_server` SKIPS these entries with the reason printed; it never fails them. `./tests/run.py --shared-server` injects the second server into every case of one run, for bringing a screen up by hand.
_fps_comment: On-device UI framerate regression scenes (./tests/run.py --fps, or --fps-player to add the player tier). Each sets its plxnative-* triggers, runs profiler-OFF, parses the once/sec `loop=<n> route=<r> fps=<n>` heartbeat for its route(+overlay), skips warmup_s samples, and requires the 2nd-lowest loop= >= loop_floor plus whichever of fps_floor / fps_ceiling the scene declares. loop= counts LOOP ITERATIONS (liveness only — a settled screen reads ~62 while swapping nothing); fps= counts FRAMES ACTUALLY SWAPPED and is the only real frame rate here. RENAMED 2026-08-01 with the old name REUSED: a pre-rename log's FPS= is this loop=, and its pres= is this fps=. `item` keys resolve through manifest.local.json exactly like the cases below; detail-transition needs an in-home-catalog (recently-added/on-deck) movie or it FAILs with 'never entered route=detail'. NOTE (who's-watching): a multi-user Plex Home roster boots to the who's-watching PICKER (route=profiles), so any home/detail scene MUST set at least one non-diagnostic plxnative-* trigger — that marks the boot automated and skips the picker to land on route=home. home-hero continuously pages the carousel with plxnative-heroosc; home-fold alternates Hero and the first shelf with plxnative-homefoldosc; home-grid starts in the grid and sweeps its rows. A scene with empty triggers stalls on the picker and FAILs with 'never entered route=home'.

fps_scenes.name: home-hero
fps_scenes.comment: Pages the real rotating Hero every 700ms, faster than the slide can become an idle screen. Both loop= and actual swapped fps= must therefore remain at least 50/s; a frozen carousel cannot pass through the idle keepalive.

fps_scenes.name: home-fold
fps_scenes.comment: Alternates the product's real Hero↔first-shelf snap every 700ms. This is the DOWN-to-cards motion the row-sweeping home-grid scene starts after and therefore could never grade.

fps_scenes.name: home-grid
fps_scenes._floor_note: homeosc is load-bearing since ui::idle landed: a STILL grid now presents ~0 frames/s by design, so an fps floor taken on one would grade the idle gate, not the grid's fill rate. Sweeping focus keeps the shelf rendering, which is what this scene is for. The still case is gated by fps:home-idle instead.
fps_scenes._fps_floor_note: Measured healthy median 41 fps on device 2026-07-31 (this scene's oscillator steps focus every 350ms and the spring now settles inside that period, so the gaps are real idle — the drop from ~60 is the settle predicate working, not a regression). fps_scenes.name: home-idle
fps_scenes.comment: The inverse of every other fps scene: it asserts the app STOPS presenting. A settled Home grid must fall to at most fps_ceiling swaps/sec (ui::idle's KEEPALIVE_MS backstop is 2s, i.e. 0.5/s, so 3 leaves room for a late poster landing without letting a regression through). `loop_floor` still applies to loop=, which counts LOOP iterations, not presents: the loop must stay alive and responsive at >=30Hz while presenting nothing. A regression that re-armed the 60Hz repaint would blow the ceiling; one that wedged the loop would blow the loop_floor. warmup_s is 8, longer than the others, because the grid keeps presenting until the last poster has landed and its reveal spring has settled.

fps_scenes.name: login-spinner
fps_scenes.comment: The purest animator test the app has. login.rs's entire Scene is {spin_ms, qr_tex} and the module contains ZERO springs, so every pixel is static except a phase-driven spinner that ui::idle cannot see structurally — before Spinner::draw was made to report, this screen drew a STOPPED spinner at 0.5 presents/s. fps_floor 30 asserts it still animates; loop_floor 30 asserts the loop is alive. plxnative-login is not in the DIAG list (app.rs), so it suppresses the boot picker on its own and no token is needed — this screen is where a user with no session lands.

fps_scenes.name: detail-transition

MEASURED on the dev set 2026-08-14: median 44 fps (min 14, max 60, n=14) with plxnative-searchosc stepping focus every 350ms. 20 is under half that median, the same margin fps:library-scroll takes (floor 25 against a 49 median) — a real regression has to halve the frame rate before this fires, and a STOPPED animator reads ~0.5/s from ui::idle's keepalive alone, so it cannot pass by freezing.

THE CARET BLINKS — this note said the opposite, quoting a ui/search/field.rs paragraph ('solid by design', 'a blinking caret would hold the GL loop awake forever') that the module itself has since retracted: BLINK_MS is 530ms and step_blink reports to ui::idle on the phase FLIP alone, so the cost is two presents a second while the panel is up and nothing while it is not. ui/search/mod.rs's the_caret_blinks_and_reports_only_on_the_flip grades both halves on the host.

What this scene grades is still not the caret, and no fps scene can: the caret is drawn only while `editing`, i.e. with the television's own keyboard raised. plxnative-search seeds the field but leaves EDITING false (search::enter calls leave() first), raising the panel takes a real OK press on the field, and run_fps_scene has no key-injection path at all — only the playback cases do, via stream_case's inject=. So a caret scene needs a harness change AND would then measure a screen with a system panel over its bottom third, which is a different measurement; the blink's gate is the host test named above.

What the fps_floor here does grade is the motion that exists while searching: the field's focus-ink fade as focus enters and leaves it, and the shelves scrolling under the sweep. A frozen shelf spring or a field that stopped reporting to ui::idle::invalidate lands here.
fps_scenes._query_note: 'th' is the one installation-DEPENDENT value in this scene, and it is a literal rather than a symbolic key because run.py resolves items, not queries. It matches any library holding titles that begin with 'The'. If YOUR library returns nothing for it the shelves are empty, the sweep has nothing to travel, and this scene degrades to grading the tab strip's focus springs — change the literal to a term your library matches rather than lowering the floor.

cases.name: auto_pin_and_back
cases.title: Auto, then PINNED to 720p·4 Mbps mid-playback, then back to Auto
cases._quality_note: THE case this family exists for, and the one a person actually performs by hand: start something on Auto, watch it, pin a rung because Auto picked something they did not want, then hand it back to Auto. Everything is real -- a real PMS, a real /decision, a real JIT encoder, a real ratingKey, real timeline scrobbles -- so what it grades is the INTEGRATION and not a model of it. No `decision` bound: on Auto the answer is the server's and the link's, and asserting one would assert whatever this library and this afternoon's network happened to agree on. What IS deterministic is the routing POLICY, and `quality_switch` grades exactly that: every requested rung produced its `quality: switch` line in order, and the ABR controller stopped when Auto stopped -- `route::hls_abr_control` returns None for any non-Auto quality, so `abr: sample` must cease after the replacement Load, and a pinned stream that kept adapting would be the app overriding a user's explicit choice. The RESUME half is graded only if this run showed Auto adapting before the first switch, because `hls_abr_control` also needs HLS delivery and a live encoder and Auto on a direct-playable item legitimately runs no controller at all -- asserting one unconditionally would fail on somebody's library for a reason that is not a defect. The trigger first observes 12 uninterrupted seconds of Playing; `gap_ms=40000` is then an explicit end-to-end test SLO: the fixed-quality replacement must load, resume playback and expose post-reload evidence within 40 s before the case hands control back to Auto. The 90 s cap leaves another 38 s after the second request for Auto's replacement and the final progress/controller evidence.

cases.name: auto_baseline
cases.title: Auto, undisturbed — the control for the switch cases
cases._quality_note: The standalone CONTROL: it establishes that playback left alone on Auto runs on this server, independently of the switching mechanism. Deliberately asserts nothing about rungs or controller presence: on an unshaped link what Auto chooses is the server's and the network's business, and a bound here would grade the afternoon. Run with `--verbose` when its `auto:` and `abr: sample` lines are wanted as characterisation; no cross-case fact is silently imported into the switch assertions.

cases.name: auto_hls_pin_and_back
cases.title: Auto HLS, then PINNED to 720p·4 Mbps, then back to Auto
cases._quality_note: The controller-forced companion to `auto_pin_and_back`. That case intentionally uses an ordinary direct-playable item and therefore cannot require an HLS controller on a Local server: Auto structurally chooses Local Original without a network probe. This case uses the existing symbolic AV1/no-direct-play-audio item, so Original is technically infeasible and Auto MUST start Fixed HLS whatever the link classification. The same switch script can therefore grade both lifecycle directions without a conditional: `abr: sample` must exist before the 4 Mbps pin, cease while fixed quality owns the route, and resume after Auto is restored. The item identity remains in the gitignored overlay. Link-specific rung assertions still belong to a netcond run; this case makes that run capable of observing the controller rather than pretending a slowed Local Original stream is ABR.

cases.name: auto_link_squeeze
cases.title: Auto over a link that collapses to 2.5 Mbps and comes back
cases._quality_note: What it does that no other server case can: it plays a REAL item off a REAL PMS over a link this harness owns, so an Auto assertion here grades the controller rather than the afternoon. The item is the AV1/no-direct-play-audio shape, so Original is infeasible and Auto must run Fixed HLS whatever the link classification says. The squeeze is 2.5 Mbps, which is below the 4000 rung and above the 2000 one, so a controller that adapts has somewhere to go and one that does not is visible as `prod` above 1000 with the rung unchanged. 50 s of unshaped link first, because the admission window needs 19 samples before it decides anything. `min_play_rate_pm` is the same product choice `auto_original_squeeze` states — 1000·(10−3)/10, one reload inside a 10-heartbeat window — and it is the assertion that would notice the controller riding an unaffordable rung instead of leaving it: measured 900 pm here, against 111 pm for the unsupervised Original path this case is the control for.

cases.name: auto_seek_after_switch
cases.title: Auto: a seek AFTER the controller has committed a rung switch

operations._mode_note: No `mode`, deliberately: this item transcodes, and a transcode seek is a REBUILD (`route::transcode_seek` -> `reload_transcode`), never an in-place `av_seek`. `mode: inplace` asserts a `seek(in-place)` line that a transcode cannot emit — it failed on device for exactly that reason, with the seek itself perfectly healthy. The default arm (`op_seek_transcode`) is the one that grades this path.

cases._quality_note: The state no other case in this suite reaches: a seek that happens AFTER the ABR controller has already committed a rung switch. It is a distinct state because `route::transcode_seek` REUSES the encoder session id deliberately — stopping it would cut the stream the demux worker is still reading — while the reload builds a fresh demux worker underneath it. So the transactions either side of a seek are the only ones whose candidate names can collide with the live session, and a client that stops its own encoder presents as a server fault: a run of 404s and `HLS segment was not produced in time`, because 404 is `NotReady` by design and the retry budget cannot tell a stopped session from a slow one. The item is the AV1/no-direct-play-audio shape, as in `auto_link_squeeze`, so Original is infeasible and Auto MUST run Fixed HLS — which is what guarantees there are transactions to collide at all. The legs are ordered to produce exactly the sequence: 40 s of unshaped link so the admission window fills, a squeeze at 40 s that forces a DOWN commit, the seek at ~87 s (12 s of route entry plus `delay_ms`), and a release at 100 s so the post-seek controller has a reason to transact again. `delay_ms` exists for this case: the app fires the first seek step at a fixed ~12 s, which on any ABR case is before the controller has ever switched. The assertion is deliberately ordinary — a dead pipeline cannot climb a timeline, and `pos=` is gated on `is_playing()`, so `min_timeline_climb_s` past the seek is what a stopped session fails.

cases.name: auto_original_squeeze
cases.title: Auto on a 10.6 Mbps direct-play source, link squeezed to 2.5 Mbps and left there
cases._quality_note: This is the shape `auto_link_squeeze` cannot reach: a Local server and a direct-playable source, where Auto chooses ORIGINAL and there is no ladder under it at all. The source is measured at 10.6 Mbps and the link is held at 2.5, a fourfold deficit, so the only escape is abandoning Original for HLS — the mode comparison, not the rung selector. The squeeze is never lifted, deliberately: the question is whether Auto ever leaves, not whether it recovers when the link does. `min_play_rate_pm` is a PRODUCT CHOICE and is labelled as one: the case permits exactly one visible mode switch, a switch is a fresh Starfish `Load`, and `playback_rate`'s window is 10 heartbeats — so a floor of 700 pm is `1000·(10−3)/10`, i.e. it tolerates one reload parking the media clock for up to three seconds inside a window and refuses anything sustained. It is DIFFERENTIAL: measured 111 pm before `auto_original_watch` stopped requiring a remote server, 818 pm after, on the same profile and the same item.

cases.name: auto_original_squeeze_released
cases.title: Auto on a 4K DoVi direct-play source: full link, squeezed, held, then released to full
cases._quality_note: The maintainer's own by-hand check, which is why it is here: play at full speed, drop the link, wait, put it back to maximum. `auto_original_squeeze` deliberately never lifts its squeeze — its question is whether Auto ever LEAVES Original — and `auto_link_squeeze` lifts one but plays the AV1/no-direct-play-audio item, where Original is infeasible and so the return can never be observed. Neither can see what a viewer reported on 2026-08-29: Auto came back to Original, left again seconds later, and the picture blinked twice on a link that was carrying the film. `max_reloads` is the assertion that exists for it, and 2 is the whole budget — one Load to leave Original when the link stops covering the source, one to come back when it recovers. Anything beyond that is a flap, and every OTHER assertion here is blind to it: a reload is brief, so climb, play rate and no-error are all satisfied throughout a flapping session. The item is a 4K DoVi direct-play source, the same shape as the reported one, so Original is genuinely reachable at the head of the run. NB the squeeze must be held long enough for the mode controller to act and the release must be to full: the band between 1.0x and 1.6875x the source is where the entry gate refuses a link that carries the film, and a release into it would grade the entry gate rather than the flap.

cases.name: original_then_auto
cases.title: Original, then handed to Auto mid-playback
cases._quality_note: The other direction, and the one with a different failure mode: a viewer whose Original playback is struggling hands it to Auto. cases._dovi_note: WHAT THIS CASE GRADES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It proves the stream TRANSPORTS: the route chose direct play, the demuxer opened it, Starfish accepted the payload, ACB bound the video plane, the timeline climbed and nothing errored. It proves NOTHING about the panel engaging Dolby Vision — no assertion here can see the picture, and `codec: hevc` is satisfied identically by a P5, a P7, a P8 and a file with no Dolby Vision at all, because it reads `avcodec_get_name`, which answers 'hevc' for every one of them. So a green run here is not evidence that DV is being displayed as DV, and it never was. What DOES distinguish them is now logged at demux open — `ff: … dovi=P8 bl_compat=1 …`, from the configuration record FFmpeg reads out of the container — and gated at the route, which since 2026-08-21 refuses to direct-play a base layer that is not self-displayable (P5, and dual-layer P7). This case is the regression guard for the OTHER side of that gate: P8.1's base layer IS HDR10, so this item must keep direct-playing exactly as before. If it ever flips to a transcode, the gate has over-reached — read metadata::Dovi::base_layer_unusable, not this file. Confirming that the panel actually lights up its Dolby Vision mode needs a human looking at the television; nothing in this suite can answer it.

_pipeline_comment: The SYNTHETIC tier, and the DEFAULT one since 2026-08-22: the player with no Plex behind it. Each case names a GENERATED clip (`make fixtures-pipeline`) served off the dev machine by tests/serve_fixtures.py, and the Load payload DECLARATION to play it with. A bare `./tests/run.py` runs them; `--server` selects the library-backed 21 instead. Nothing here is installation-dependent -- no ratingKey, no PMS, no token, no manifest.local.json -- which is what makes this the tier a stranger can run.
_pipeline_declare_comment: `declare` is written verbatim into /tmp/plxnative-playurl (the harness injects `url`) and lands in route::set_stream_declaration, i.e. it IS the Load payload: `vcodec` picks the H265 vs H264 payload, `acodec` is renamed LG-side (eac3 -> "AC3 PLUS", aac -> "AAC", everything else -> "AC3"), `dovi` becomes the contents.DolbyHdrInfo node and `atmos` the contents.immersive one. `expect.load_*` grades what the app SAYS; `expect.codec` / `audio_stream_index` grade what the demuxer FOUND. The two are independent here, which is the whole point -- on the integration tier they both come from the same PMS metadata and can only ever agree.
_pipeline_skip_comment: A fixture the pack does not hold SKIPS its cases with the reason printed, exactly as an unresolvable `item` does on the integration tier. So does a fixture generated SHORTER than the case seeks into it (checked with ffprobe), which would otherwise fail as though the player had regressed.
_resolution_matrix_comment:
LG App Self Checklist #50 / #51 is graded as a MATRIX of resolution x codec, and until 2026-08-23 this repo could only answer it as "pieces are covered": every fixture was 1080p except one 4K HEVC, so SD and HD had never been played at all and 4K H.264 existed in neither pack. The eight cells, all direct-play, all 24p, one audio codec per column so a row-to-row difference is the RESOLUTION and nothing else:

                    h264 / AC-3 5.1 mkv     hevc / E-AC-3 5.1 mkv
  SD    720x480     pipe_res_h264_sd        pipe_res_hevc_sd
  HD   1280x720     pipe_res_h264_hd        pipe_res_hevc_hd
  FHD  1920x1080    pipe_h264_ac3_1080p     pipe_res_hevc_fhd
  UHD  3840x2160    pipe_res_h264_uhd       pipe_hevc_eac3_4k_hdr10

Two cells predate the matrix and keep their names (`covers` carries `resolution-matrix` on them, so grepping that tag finds all eight). Every cell grades `expect.video_size` — an EXACT WxH out of the `ff:` line's AVCodecParameters, not a `min_video_width`, which cannot tell 720x480 from 720x576 and is how a matrix gets answered with "at least 1900 wide". The UHD/HEVC cell is HDR10 Main10 where every other cell is SDR 8-bit: HDR is a third axis, that cell is the one already device-verified (2026-08-22), and an SDR twin would differ from it only in `trc=`/`pri=`, which nothing here grades. Uncovered on purpose: the 4096-wide edge the device table claims and any refusal above it, and every non-24p rung (the frame-rate axis is pipe_h264_1080p5994 and pipe_hevc_4k_60fps, both at 1080p/4K only).

pipeline_cases._eof_note: One of the TWO cases in either tier that are supposed to run out — the other is `pipe_replay_after_eos` — and between them the only two allowed to name `pipe_h264_ac3_short.mkv`. Every other clip in both packs is sized so it CANNOT hit EOF inside a case's window (make_fixtures.py trap 9's second half), because a finish tears the session down under assertions that were only ever about playing; the rule is not "one case" but "a case graded through a teardown has to have declared `reaches_eos`", which tests/test_harness.py pins. run_secs is 60 against a 20 s clip: _resolve_fixtures SKIPS a `reaches_eos` case when the fixture is longer than 0.6 * run_secs PER VIEWING, so a pack regenerated with --secs/--quick skips it instead of failing it as a player regression.
pipeline_cases._replay_note: #46's REPLAY half is `pipe_replay_after_eos` below, which plays this same clip, lets it end, and starts it again. This case stays separate and grades the FINISH alone: the two failures are different — a stream that never ends, and a stream that ends and cannot be restarted — and collapsing them into one case would report either as the other.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_replay_after_eos
pipeline_cases.title: the same 20 s clip played to its end and then STARTED AGAIN — LG #46
pipeline_cases._replay_note: LG App Self Checklist #46, both halves, and the ONE case in either tier that plays the same media twice in one boot. `expect.replays` is the whole mechanism: the harness writes it into `/tmp/plxnative-replay`, and `app.rs` re-arms its one-shot `auto_tried` latch that many times when a `plxnative-playurl` playback reaches EOS — so the number the app is told and the number `a_replayed` grades cannot drift apart. A COUNTER rather than a lifted latch, because `auto_tried` also guards the autoplay+playidx arm, which fetches a catalog item; an unconditionally re-armable latch would loop a real playback forever.
pipeline_cases._wire_note: `server_opens_min: 2` is not decoration and is the assertion no log line can give. The second playback must fetch the clip AGAIN — `teardown` closed the socket and cleared the URL — so a 'replay' that somehow reused the first session's bytes would still satisfy the two `load:` lines and the position drop, and would be caught here, on the fixture server's own counter. It is a floor, not an equality: a `Range` reopen inside either viewing is permitted.
pipeline_cases._climb_note: `a_replayed` wants the position to FALL and then climb, which is the only signal that separates a restart from a session that carried on. A `min_pos_climb_s` of 8 alone cannot see it: one 20 s viewing satisfies that on its own, which is why the drop is asserted separately rather than by raising the climb floor to 30.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_auto_original_slow_recover
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: Original -> 4 Mbps collapse -> HLS -> recovered Original
pipeline_cases._network_note: The fixture server starts its phase clock on the first response body, not app launch: 40 Mbps permits Original to establish, 4 Mbps drains an 8 Mbps source until the starvation horizon closes and the risk model replaces it, then 40 Mbps gives the real HLS controller enough segment/network/production headroom to climb while a bounded source probe re-measures the actual file. Recovery is decided by the probe's uncertainty-discounted rate against the source's VBR-adjusted requirement, NOT by reaching a particular rung first, so the rung the ladder happens to be on when the probe fires is not graded. The four pipe_abr_* two-second files are independently decodable candidate segments; no Plex token, library item, decision endpoint or transcoder participates.
pipeline_cases._window_note: run_secs is 140 rather than 80 because the recovery this case GRADES provably cannot complete in 80 s, which made the bound unfalsifiable rather than strict. Device-measured 2026-08-28: the collapse phase drains the reserve for real, and `BufferEstimate::slope_ms_per_s` is a 3:1 EWMA, so once the link returns the reserve sits pinned at B_max(6000) (flat at ~15.5 s) while the slope decays -1822 -> -88 -> -66 -> -49 against `DRAIN_EPS_MS_PER_S` of 50. `OriginalRecovery::probe_due` resets its spacing timer on every `!refilling` reading, so no probe can be due until that clears, and then `probe_spacing_ms` still has to accumulate. At 80 s the run ended ONE sample short: `load_count` saw 2 of 3 and the log's last line was `abr: probe withheld reason=draining ... slope=-66`. At 140 s the same binary recovers Original and `load_count` passes. This is NOT slack for a flaky case -- `run_secs` is a cap and this case declares no `abr_shape`, so early exit applies and a passing run costs what it needs. Raising it makes the window long enough to OBSERVE the graded event; it does not make the assertion weaker.
pipeline_cases._recovery_link_note: The recovery leg is 44000, and it is DERIVED rather than chosen. The probe reads the source CONCURRENTLY with the HLS stream (`probe_due` demands a deep reserve precisely because the probe spends the link the segments need) and `serve_fixtures.py`'s bucket is SHARED, so two concurrent transfers get half each. The probe's ceiling is therefore link/2, and asserting `abr_recovery_min_kbps: 20000` requires link > 40000 -- AT exactly 40000 the ceiling equals the bound and the probe can only measure the scheduling loss below it (device 19917, host 19856, i.e. 0.4-0.7%). 44000 gives the probe 22000, a 10% margin, more than ten times the measured loss. The BOUND is untouched: the link was the wrong parameter, not the assertion. NB raising the link was tried once before and appeared to fail -- at 48000 the ladder climbs to rung 20000 and the recovery gate reported `shallow_reserve` -- but that was the un-derived `deep_reserve = 3 * segment` (6000 ms) exceeding B_max at the top rung. With the gate derived from the probe's own budget (4000 ms, under the sweep's 5293 ms floor at that rung) the top of the ladder recovers normally; measured `source probe 23895kbps; recovered direct play` at 48000 and 21969 at 44000.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_slow_start_then_fast
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: 2 Mbps start -> 40 Mbps link, climbing by SKIPPING rungs
pipeline_cases._run_secs_note: 150 rather than 90, DERIVED from the plant this case grades rather than fitted to the number that came back. `floor_kbps: 10000` needs three commits from the 720 seed (720 -> 2000 -> 8000 -> above 10000), and each one needs the acquisition window to reach n_min = k/eps - 1 = 19 samples at 2 s of media per segment -- about 38 s per step plus the transaction, so roughly 120 s for three. A 90 s cap could not admit the third, which means the bound was only ever satisfiable through an estimate no measurement supported: until `CapacityObservation::quality` applied its interval floor to every tier, one large-but-brief transfer read as tens of millions of kbps and the ladder jumped on it. With that fixed the same 90 s window settles at 8000 with max_stall_s=0 and play_rate_pm=1000 -- healthy, and short of the bound. `run_secs` is a CAP and a passing case exits at its last assertion, so raising it costs nothing when the case passes.
pipeline_cases._network_note: The plan's rung-SKIPPING requirement, graded directly. A 60 Mbit/s source can never be Original here, so Auto is in HLS from the first segment; the link then opens by a factor of twenty. The 13-point catalog means walking it would cost eight or nine encoder transactions, each a visible quality change and each a separately named PMS session -- so `max_commits: 5` is the assertion, and `floor_kbps` is what stops a controller that simply refuses to climb from passing it. Both bounds are needed: either alone is satisfiable by doing nothing.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_steady_modest_link
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: a flat 6 Mbps link is not spent like a 40 Mbps one
pipeline_cases._network_note: The OVERREACH guard, and the only case here that can fail on the controller being too eager rather than too timid. A client that spends a 6 Mbit/s link reaching for 20 still plays -- it rebuffers, recovers, and passes every other assertion in this file -- so `ceiling_kbps` is the assertion no position climb can stand in for. `floor_kbps` pins the other side: it must still leave the 720 Kbps bootstrap rung, or 'never overreached' is trivially true.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_uhd_source_admits_4k
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: a 4K source on a fast link reaches the Uhd rung
pipeline_cases._uhd_note: The ONE case that can reach the Uhd actuator, and the plan's I9 blocker made runnable. Every other auto_network case declares a 1080p source, so `HlsActuatorCatalog::limited_to` deletes Uhd before anything is scored -- which meant the two `production_load_pm` entries the table calls EMPIRICAL (the 1080p anchor at 1000 and Uhd at 2100) were the two no case on any tier could exercise. Three things had to change together and none is a policy: `tests/serve_fixtures.py` now answers rung 22000 with a real 3840x2160 clip (it served none, so a candidate 404'd and read as a rejected encoder); `route::arm_auto_fixture` takes the source raster instead of hardcoding 1080p (the literal was there BECAUSE of the 404); and a case can declare it. `floor_kbps: 22000` is the assertion that matters and it is the Uhd rung ITSELF -- `floor_kbps` means some rung at or above this was ACTIVE, so nothing below 4K satisfies it. A `settle_min_kbps: 20000` alone would have been a false pass: settling on P1080High (20000) clears it while proving nothing about Uhd, which is the exact hole this case exists to close. The pair says reached-and-stayed-high. This is the half no existing case grades: every other abr_shape here bounds the controller from ABOVE. The 60 Mbit/s leg is well above the 22 Mbit/s rung so the link is not the binding constraint -- if this fails, the catalog or the acceptance test is.
pipeline_cases._declare_note: The fixture is the ABR ladder's OWN 4K clip, and that is the point rather than a convenience. The harness checks a case's `declare` against the streams the fixture really carries, and it must ALSO match what is actually decoded — which under `start_hls` is the ladder, never the Original. A 4K source with AC-3 audio (`pipe_h264_ac3_2160p.mkv`, the resolution matrix's clip) satisfies neither reading at once: declaring `ac3` makes the engine describe a stream it is not playing, and declaring `aac` is refused by the fixture check. `pipe_h264_aac_2160p.mkv` is 3840x2160 H.264 + AAC at full length, so the source raster, the fixture's own streams and the ladder all agree. It is NOT `pipe_abr_4k_22m.ts`, which was tried and skipped: that is a LADDER clip whose unsuffixed file is segment 0 alone, two seconds, and a source has to outlast the case's own `min_pos_climb_s`. This case had it as the matrix clip for one run and skipped. Historic note: AAC, not the AC3 and the mismatch is correct rather than sloppy. With `start_hls` the app never plays the Original at all -- the fixture is there to be the 4K SOURCE, which is what makes the Uhd rung feasible, and every byte actually decoded comes from the ABR ladder, which is AAC at every rung. The Load declaration describes the stream being played. This case had it as `ac3` for one run and the engine correctly logged `a="AAC"`; the expectation was wrong, not the app.
pipeline_cases._raster_note: `hls_raster_within` grades the decoded picture against the rung's BOX, not against equality, so a 22000 rung serving a 1080p clip would be admitted and would prove nothing. The fixture is generated at 3840x2160 for that reason and the server asserts the raster alongside it.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_brief_dropout
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: a 3 s near-stall mid-stream, then full speed again
pipeline_cases._network_note: A transient, which is the shape an EWMA gets wrong in both directions: too much memory and the 200 Kbps window is ignored until the buffer is gone, too little and the link is written off for the rest of the film. The assertion is the RECOVERY (`settle_min_kbps`), because the downshift itself is easy and correct -- what the regime-change reset in `CapacityEstimate::update` exists for is making sure one 200 Kbps observation does not stay blended into the estimate afterwards. Verified in the same run by `no_playing_error`: the reserve is supposed to absorb three seconds.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_oscillating_link
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: a link flipping 20/3 Mbps must not flip the picture with it
pipeline_cases._network_note: Five link changes in 44 s. A controller with no transition cost tracks every one of them, which is five to ten visible quality changes to the person watching and five to ten separately named PMS encoder sessions -- correct by every instantaneous measure and wrong as a product. `max_commits` grades the DECAYING switch penalty (`visible_switch_penalty` halving every `visible_switch_decay_ms`): the first move is cheap, the fourth inside two minutes has to buy a lot. It is deliberately not 1 -- refusing to move at all on a link that really does collapse is the opposite failure, and `no_playing_error` plus the position climb are what stop that passing.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_pin_320
pipeline_cases.title: M4 census: hold request=320 kbps and read the settled reserve
pipeline_cases._census_note: Measurement step M4 of docs/adaptive-playback-plan.md, as ONE command: this case writes the play URL, quality=auto and plxnative-abrpin together, so the census needs no manual prerequisite. the bottom of the ladder: the 1 MiB AUDIO queue should bind, not the 8 MiB video one. The link is deliberately UNSHAPED (no network_profile) so the AU queue byte cap is the only limiter -- a shaped leg would measure the shaper instead. `start_hls` is what puts this case in HLS, and it is the honest replacement for what used to: `source_kbps: 900000` was declared so that the starvation horizon would fire and drop Auto out of Original, on an unshaped link where the reserve was visibly FILLING. That entry only ever worked because the horizon did not check whether anything was draining, and it stopped working the day that was fixed -- correctly, since a growing reserve is not a starvation. `route::arm_auto_fixture` now installs the post-fallback state directly. The declared rate is kept because it still bounds the actuator raster and keeps Original RECOVERY out of the case, and it no longer forces anything. `abr_shape: {}` reports every I0 metric and asserts none of them: this case exists to produce evidence, and a bound written before the baseline exists would be a number somebody guessed. Run it with --no-early: the census needs the FULL window, and a case that satisfied every assertion would otherwise stop as soon as it had. min_pos_climb_s stays below the 60 s entry fixture's own duration, which the harness checks up front.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_pin_720
pipeline_cases.title: M4 census: hold request=720 kbps and read the settled reserve
pipeline_cases._shaped_reason: HISTORICAL: the pin needed six segments of reserve in BOTH directions until 2026-08-27 and so could not transact down from the ladder top. It needs two going down now and the P2 census landed every unshaped pin, so this flat leg is a leftover rather than a requirement
pipeline_cases._census_note: Measurement step M4 of docs/adaptive-playback-plan.md, as ONE command: this case writes the play URL, quality=auto and plxnative-abrpin together, so the census needs no manual prerequisite. the bootstrap rung, still predicted AUDIO-bound. This point carries a FLAT 6000 kbps leg, and that departure is now HISTORICAL: unshaped, the link measures 84-111 Mbit/s and `startup_rung` picks the top rung, and until 2026-08-27 the pin could not transact down from there because PIN_MIN_RESERVE_SEGMENTS charged an UPSHIFT derivation of six segments in both directions -- 12000 ms against a ceiling of ~5421. It charges two going down now (PIN_MIN_RESERVE_SEGMENTS_DOWN), and the P2 census landed this pin unshaped, so the leg is a leftover the next census can drop. pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_band_4000
pipeline_cases.title: M4 census: hold request=4000 and sweep the link through the unobserved A/D band
pipeline_cases._band_note: The ONE region no measurement has ever entered: `A/D` in [0.80, 1.05], 0 of 366 samples in the entire pre-existing corpus, and the boundary the whole admission rule is keyed on. A pin holds the rung while the SHAPER sweeps the link, so `A/D` is swept directly instead of being waited for. Every leg rate is DERIVED, not chosen: from this rung's own measured (bytes, A, C) the fixed cost is A - 8*bytes/C, which is link-independent (p2h R27: ~79% of acquisition lands after the first AU, serial and post-body), so the rate producing a target A/D is 8*bytes / (target*D - fixed). The pin is what makes this safe to hold past 1.0: it short-circuits the decision before the fast-down path, so the controller cannot escape the rung and the drain is bounded by the leg length. At A/D = 1.05 a 2 s segment takes 2.1 s, draining 100 ms per segment, so a 20 s leg costs ~1 s of reserve -- inside B_max at both rungs. `abr_shape: {}` reports every metric and asserts none: a bound written before the band has ever been observed would be a number somebody guessed. Rung 4000: measured bytes ~1 070 000 and A ~700 ms at a 20 000 kbps shaper give a fixed cost of 272 ms, so 6446 / 5602 / 4683 kbps are A/D = 0.80 / 0.90 / 1.05 exactly. pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_reject_up_4000
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: an upshift the candidate cannot pay for, rejected repeatedly
pipeline_cases._reject_note: Measures E_tx(up, reject) -- the cost of an upshift that is PROPOSED and then REFUSED -- which the plan ranks 4th among the device cases and which today has n=1, unlabelled. The flat 8300 kbps leg is DERIVED, not chosen, and it is the only leg in this file that has to sit inside a window rather than above or below a threshold. `candidate_prime_budget` gives the candidate 4/5 of one media duration, 1600 ms. From the measured fixed cost of 272 ms and the rungs' own median segment bytes (1.07 MB at 4000, 1.50 MB at 6000): at 8300 kbps rung 4000 costs 1303 ms, comfortably sustainable at A/D 0.65 so the controller stays there and keeps proposing, while rung 6000's warm-up costs 1718 ms and overruns its budget, so every proposal is rejected. The window has a far edge and it is worth knowing where: at 10000 kbps the candidate costs 1472 ms and is ACCEPTED, so a link 20% faster turns this case into an upshift test instead. The opening 15 s at 40000 kbps is NOT decoration and the case does not work without it: device-observed 2026-08-27, a flat 8300 kbps leg starts the controller low and `slow_kbps` is an 8-weight EWMA, so it CLIMBS toward the true link instead of sitting at it -- 4830 then 5031 over a 120 s window, with `conservative` = 5031*0.8 = 4025 only just reaching rung 4000's boundary as the run ended. The instantaneous observation was fine throughout (`net` 6426-7908), so this is EWMA convergence and not a measurement error. Opening fast makes the estimate DESCEND to 8300 rather than climb to it, which puts the controller at 4000 within the window instead of after it. `settle_max_kbps: 4000` is the assertion that matters -- if the rejection path breaks, Auto commits to 6000 on a link that cannot carry it and this fails. No `max_stall_s`, deliberately: a stall bound is what this case most wants to assert -- repeated rejected transactions draining the reserve is the exact failure E_tx exists to bound -- but `max_stall_s` is an I0 metric and `test_no_manifest_case_carries_a_new_abr_bound_yet` refuses it until an I1 baseline exists. That guard is right and asserting 0 here would have been the guessed number it was written to stop. The metric is still REPORTED, so this run is what produces the baseline that lets a later increment assert it.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_down_collapse
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: a sustained link collapse, and the full descent it forces
pipeline_cases._collapse_note: Measures E_tx_down under collapse -- the plan's 5th-ranked device case, and the one that matters most because it is where the descent is priced. It was written when DOWNSHIFTS HAD NO DEADLINE AT ALL (`candidate_prime_budget` and `candidate_warmup_budget` both returned None for Direction::Down), and it is the case that produced the evidence: one warm-up fetch of 36 156 ms against a 5 793 ms reserve, which is 6.2x the reserve it was spending. Since J3b (2026-08-27) a candidate transfer is bounded by that reserve in both directions, so this case now measures the descent WITH the bound in place -- and `warmup_dl=` on each `abr: tx` line says what the bound was, which is the field that lets a captured log state whether it held rather than only how long the fetch took. The 500 kbps floor is derived rather than picked: at that rate only rung 320 is sustainable (A/D 0.90 from the measured fixed cost and rung 320's own 380 kbps of media), while 720 is at 1.74 and 2000 at 4.58 -- so the controller has to walk the WHOLE ladder down from the top rung an unshaped start puts it on, which is what makes the descent cost observable rather than inferred. Distinct from `pipe_abr_brief_dropout`, which dips for 3 s and grades the RECOVERY: this one holds the floor for the rest of the run and grades the descent. `settle_max_kbps: 720` is deliberately one rung looser than the arithmetic demands -- the assertion is that the full descent happens, not that it lands on exactly the rung a model predicts, since a model that also chose the leg rate would be marking its own work. No `max_stall_s`: a collapse from the ladder top through a ~4.9 s reserve may legitimately stall, and asserting it must not would be asserting a result nobody has measured.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_down_staircase
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: a TWO-STEP collapse, the shape that outruns a downshift
pipeline_cases._staircase_note: RECONSTRUCTS the one pathological transaction in the corpus, and makes it deterministic. `pipe_abr_down_collapse` produced a 36 156 ms warm-up fetch against a 5 793 ms reserve ONCE IN THREE RUNS OF THE SAME CASE (6.24x in j3a-window-logs; 0.64x in p2-logs and 0.74x in j3b-logs), so it cannot be used to grade a transfer deadline: two of three runs never enter the state. Reading the three timelines side by side says why. The single cliff 40000 -> 500 is measured by the sample that straddles it, and WHICH rate that sample reports decides everything: p2 and j3b measured ~500 and targeted rung 320, whose segment fetches in ~1.4 s at 500 kbps; j3a measured the INTERMEDIATE 9593, targeted rung 8000, and then fetched a ~2 MB segment at the 500 kbps floor -- 32 s of transfer against a 5.8 s reserve. Whether the straddling sample reads 9593 or 500 is a coincidence of where the fetch boundary falls, which is why the case is intermittent. The middle leg here MAKES that reading deterministic: a full sample at 9600 forces a downshift target the floor cannot carry, and the drop to 500 lands inside its warm-up fetch. 22 s is far enough in for the ladder to have climbed and the reserve to have filled; 9600 is the measured value from the pathological run rather than a round number. What this case grades is unchanged from its sibling -- the descent completes (`settle_max_kbps`) without a `Playing error` -- because the DEADLINE is not gradeable by an assertion here: it is visible as `warmup_dl=` and a `warmup_deadline` outcome on the `abr: tx` line, and asserting an outcome would pin a mechanism rather than a behaviour. No `max_stall_s`, for the same reason as `pipe_abr_down_collapse`: a collapse through a ~5 s reserve may legitimately stall, and asserting otherwise would assert a result nobody has measured.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_down_outrun
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: a link that falls UNDER a downshift already in flight
pipeline_cases._outrun_index_note: The INDICES were re-derived on 2026-08-28; the note below still describes the mechanism correctly but no longer the arithmetic, and two of its premises were stale. (1) It opens "segment 0 is the seed rung 10000" — the seed comes from `route::cur_ceiling()` and is P720Low, which a case cannot pin, so ten segments in the controller is still on 720 and has climbed nothing. (2) It wants a reserve near 9 s so the warm-up deadline can bind, and `candidate_warmup_budget(Down, ..)` IS the reserve — but ten segments in the reserve is tens of seconds deep and any fetch fits inside it. Both were measured off a real request stream, which is what the note itself asks for: on a 720 seed the acquisition window admits a commit every ~19 media responses (observed at global segments 22, 40 and 59 of `pipe_abr_slow_start_then_fast`), and the reserve is THIN only just after a climb — 58751 ms at the second commit against 12046 ms at the third. The condition this case needs therefore sits shortly after the third commit. Device-verified 2026-08-28: segment 61 served at 6000 triggers `Down 18000->2000`, and segment 62 — that candidate's warm-up, served at 500 against a 2168 ms reserve — returns `outcome=warmup_deadline`, which is the event this case exists for and which no run had ever produced. `run_secs` is 200 rather than 150 because the deadline landed on the LAST media response of a 150 s window: the graded behaviour is the descent COMPLETING after it, so the window has to outlast the event it triggers. **THIS CASE IS EXPECTED TO FAIL TODAY, and that is why it is kept.** With the shaper armed and the indices right it reproduces, deterministically and for the first time, the defect the whole Auto effort exists for: at rung 18000 against a 500 kbps link one segment is ~4.5 MB = 36 Mbit, i.e. 72 s of fetch — and the controller observes only on segment COMPLETION, so for those 72 s it receives no sample and can decide nothing. Measured 2026-08-28: max_stall_s=72, play_rate_pm=620, settled 18000. The warm-up deadline DOES fire and abandons the candidate correctly; what is missing is any action on the CURRENT rung's own fetch, which is the one taking 72 s. That is the plan's abort rule (R16's `t_remaining` projection) and `must_downshift`'s missing terminal case (R12), neither of which is built. Do not weaken the bound to make this green — a settled 18000 with the picture at 62% of real time is the exact behaviour the owner reported as unacceptable. None of it mattered before 2026-08-28, because `tests/run.py` never called `set_segment_profile`: the shaper was implemented in `serve_fixtures.py` and covered by `test_harness.py`, and the runner armed only its wall-clock sibling — so this case streamed over an unshaped link and could not pass by construction.
pipeline_cases._outrun_note: The ONLY case that can make a candidate transfer deadline fire, and it needs the REQUEST-INDEXED shaper (`segment_profile`) rather than the wall-clock one. The reason is structural rather than a matter of tuning: the controller chooses its downshift target from the rate it just measured, and admits a rung only if its expected_wire_kbps fits that budget -- so on any steady link one segment of the target fetches in about one segment of time and no deadline can bind. A transfer only becomes unaffordable when the rate underneath it drops AFTER the choice was made. With a wall-clock cliff that is a PHASE relationship (the cliff must land near the end of a segment fetch, so the measurement stays high and the next fetch runs slow), which is why `pipe_abr_down_collapse` produced it exactly once in three runs of the same case and why `pipe_abr_down_staircase` did not produce it at all. Keyed to the segment COUNT the same event is exact. Every index is read off a real request stream rather than guessed: segment 0 is the seed rung 10000, the controller downshifts to 8000 at segment 1 and holds it through segment 15 while the S4 admission window fills (19 samples), and the reserve is full from segment 4. So segment 10 sits mid-stretch at rung 8000 with ~10 s of reserve: served at 6000 it is below what rung 8000 needs, which triggers a downshift, and the budget it leaves selects rung 4000. Segment 11 IS that candidate's warm-up, served at 500 -- and rung 4000 carries 4386 kbps of media, so 2 s of it is 8772 kbit, which at 500 kbps is 17.5 s against a deadline of roughly the 9.2 s reserve. The arithmetic is the case. 500 is the same floor `pipe_abr_down_collapse` uses and is not chosen against the threshold: it is low enough that rung 4000 cannot be fetched and high enough that rung 320 can (752 kbit in 1.5 s), so the descent still has somewhere to land. What is GRADED stays the behaviour -- the descent completes, nothing errors -- because asserting `warmup_deadline` would pin a mechanism; the deadline is read from `warmup_dl=` and the outcome on the `abr: tx` line. No `max_stall_s`: at 500 kbps the CURRENT rung cannot be fetched either, so a stall here is the link, not the controller.

pipeline_cases.name: pipe_abr_seek_flat
pipeline_cases.title: no-Plex Auto: a REFUSED seek must not latch the read-out
pipeline_cases._seek_note: The one case in either tier that SEEKS while Auto is running, and it changed purpose after its first run -- which is recorded rather than tidied away, because the run is why the case is worth keeping. It was written for R11: a seek clears SHARED.hls_audio_tail_ns, so the first segment after one can present an A/V session whose audio lane has produced no timestamp, and `BufferSnapshot::buffered_ms` answered 0 for that until R11, which the emergency trigger reads as an EMPTY reserve. It cannot serve that purpose HERE and the reason is structural: a transcode seek restarts the encode at a new &offset, `route::transcode_seek` builds that from a PMS ratingKey and client, and a plxnative-playurl playback has neither -- so the seek is refused before any segment is fetched. The `unreadable reserve: n/N` characterisation line still reports whether the R11 branch was reached; it reads 0/37, and R11 stays host-proven and device-unobserved. What the first run DID find is a real defect, which is now what this case grades. `request_seek` arms SHARED.seeking and, before 2026-08-27, only a successful prime->Play ever disarmed it -- so the refusal latched PlaybackState::Seeking permanently: a spinner over the picture, the playhead frozen at 40 s, and pos= absent from every later heartbeat, while 37 further segments were acquired, four rung commits landed and the loop held 60 fps for 84 more seconds. The stream was fine; only the app's account of it was stuck. `seek_refused` asserts the position advances AFTER the refusal line, which is exactly what a latched spinner prevents, so the assertion is differential against the code that produced it. `floor_kbps` stays because a refused seek must also leave the CONTROLLER alone -- Auto is still high on a flat 40 Mbps link afterwards.

This line used to say the mp4 container gate made it unreachable, which stopped being true on 2026-08-11 when .mp4/.m4v joined .mkv — for those ten days a P5 file direct-played and displayed in wrong colours, and nothing here could notice, because the codec assertion reads avcodec_get_name and that says 'hevc' for every Dolby Vision profile alike. A case here must grade the OUTPUT and not the decision: measured against the dev PMS 2026-08-21, refusing direct play returned Part.decision=transcode with the VIDEO stream's own decision 'copy' and DOVIProfile 5 still on it — the same bitstream one container down, which an assertion on 'decision: transcode' would have passed over. The route now also withdraws the copy permission (TranscodeSpec::no_video_copy) and this server answers general code 2000, 'File is unplayable. DoVi (Profile 5) color space is not supported.' — so the honest expectation for this item is the failure read-out, not a playing stream)
